newsitem.title: USA: New York fashion week shows the familiar and the odd.
newsitem.headline: New York fashion week shows the familiar and the odd.

text.p: New York City's fashion week, which kicks off on Saturday with Japanese designer Yoshyuki Kionishi's "Asian dandy"-inspired show, follows closely on the heels of the Milan and Paris shows and will undoubtedly echo them.

The dominant trends in the last month's European shows -- '80's-style fashions, hot young designers and more intimate venues -- are expected to grab the spotlight in the New York fashion gala as well.
Models will sport trousers in masculine suit fabrics, gray and black jackets with shoulder pads, and stiletto heels, all throwbacks to the power suiits of the past decade.
Designers also are playing with '70's-style asymmetrical cuts and decidedly '90's ethnic-inspired motifs popular in this year's spring collections.

The 7th on Sixth organisation, the central coordinator of New York City fashion shows since 1993, will also see more designers follow the lead of Calvin Klein, Ralph Lauren and Donna Karan and stage their runway shows outside of the organiser's designated venues.

Anna Sui will unveil her Gothic-tinged fall fashions in an uptown church, while costume designer Bob Mackie, a long-time 7th on Sixth participant, will preview his collection on the set of the hit musical "Chicago" at a Broadway theatre.
Around the city, many lesser-known but ultra-trendy New York designers such as Spooky, Daryl K, and Yumthing will also be previewing their newest creations independently of the mainstage events.
There are 16 first-time presenters at 7th on Sixth this year, including Kionishi and American classic design house Halston.

Beyond the novelty and the independent spirit, however, there are some constants in every season's fashion preview -- tall models with tiny waists and long legs and celebrity-laden, fashion-conscious audiences to dominate the shows.
